Short answer: yes, I have almost everything, with one real blocker. The work, specs and rules the handoff points to all exist. The handoff names the Design System artifact but doesn't say how to open it or where `tokens.json` is inside it. I worked that out and read it.

**What I checked**
- The worktree `JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign` is on `claude/composer-redesign` at `170d1ae080`. The uncommitted files match the handoff's list, and the worktree has its own `build/arm64` and `node_modules`.
- Both Figma spec files are in the local figma-mirror folder. The proposal spec was updated today.
- `design-system.md`, `fork-stewardship.md` and `handoff-design-token-sync.md` all exist.

**What's missing or unclear**
1. **The token sync has to come first, and it hasn't been done.** Step 1 says the composer can't use the Figma sizes until the shared design tokens are updated. Those are the tokens in `design-tokens.json` that every screen reads. My guess is the sync hasn't started: its handoff is still untracked and I found no token-sync branch or worktree. I haven't confirmed that with whoever owns it. The token-sync handoff also has its own open questions for you, such as what to do with colours that exist only in the code. So I need you to decide: do the sync here first, or wait for another session to do it.
2. **The provider, model and thinking-level pickers need a conversation with you first.** The handoff says so itself, so that's expected. Steps 2, 3 and 5 (focus ring, native file picker, build and screenshots) don't depend on anything else.
3. **One small ambiguity about the focus ring.** The artifact's `border-focus` token says "2px ring, offset 2px". The Composer component draws the 2px stroke on the box's own edge. I'd follow the Composer component unless you say otherwise.

**Getting into the artifact**
The handoff gives only the URL (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the bare filename `tokens.json`. That filename doesn't work as a path: reading it fails. The file is actually at `project/tokens.json`. I found that by listing the artifact's files with the Artifact tool, then read it. The token-sync handoff, unlike this one, also names a local copy at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.

Two things to know about what's in the artifact:
- **`tokens.json` doesn't hold the control sizes this task needs.** It has colours, spacing, radius, shadows and five component sizes. The icon button's 32 px and the menu row's 36 px aren't in it. Those come from the Figma components, through the local spec files.
- **The artifact's Composer description is the old design.** It describes a 50 px entry with an "Attach a file" link, not the + menu. That fits the handoff's note that the artifacts haven't been re-synced, so the spec files are the current design source, not the artifact.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

I need two answers, medium thoroughness:

A) For each of these design-system components, report what the CODE actually renders (height, padding, gap, radius, and which token or literal it comes from), separately for native (wx) and for each web page (AgentUI, HomeUI), with file:line:
1. Link button (text-only underlined action, e.g. "‹ Back", "Open printer settings"). In AgentUI look at `button.link` (styles.css ~1635) and `.panel-link-button` (~2670). Figma: 26 high, padding 0 vertical / 4 horizontal, radius 4, text Label Bold (12/16 bold).

3. Segmented control. Figma: 30 high, padding 2, radius 4, segments 24 high with padding 4/16, radius 4, text Label (12/16).
4. Tooltip. Figma: 24 high, padding 4/8, radius 4, fill neutral ink, text Metadata (10/14), elevation subtle. Note native tooltips may be the OS's own wxToolTip; say so if so.
5. Sheet / dialog (Dialog/Confirmation in AgentUI styles.css ~685, the printer dialog natively). Figma: padding 24, gap 16, radius 12, elevation strong.
6. Primary and secondary buttons: confirm the rendered height. Figma: primary 34 high (padding 8/16, text 13/18 bold), secondary 32 high (padding 6/12, 1px border, text 13/18). Report whether the code fixes a height or derives it from padding + line height + border.

B) For each of these tokens, list every consumer (file:line, native and web, plus tests that assert the value, e.g. tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp and AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts): component.button.icon (26x26), component.menuRow (height 32, radius 4, sideInset 4), component.popover (paddingY 4, rowGap 0, radius 8), component.chip (height 26), dimension.radius.pill (9999), primitive.status.successDark / dangerDark / warningDark (and the dark semantic status colours). Report concisely as tables. Label anything you inferred rather than read.

159:## Writing UI code
160-
161-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
162-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
163-the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
164-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
165-
166-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
167-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
168-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
169-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
170-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
171-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
172-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
173-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
174-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
175-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
176-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
177-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
178-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
179-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
180-   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
181-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
182-3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
183-   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
184-   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
185-4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
186-   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
187-   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
188-5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
189-   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
190-   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
191-   token file records what stayed.
192-6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
193-   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
194-   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,

197-   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;

result.output:
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
  type: feedback

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
  type: project

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
  type: feedback

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

input.caption: Header printer menu drawn by the app itself. A is today's sizes (the ones you kept on 2026-09-07). B is Figma's sizes. Light and dark.

content.text:
I've finished comparing the code's design tokens (the size and colour values in `design-tokens.json`) with Figma. Most of the differences I can just fix, since you ruled that Figma wins. Four need your decision before I change anything, and the header menu is the biggest. Nothing has been changed yet.

**The header menu.** The two pictures above show the printer menu at both sets of sizes. The app drew them itself, because macOS blocks screen capture from here. A is today's sizes, the ones you kept when you reverted the Figma restyle on 2026-09-07. B is Figma's: chip 28, rows 36 at full width, padding 8, a 2 px gap between rows. Three things to know about B:
- The same menu size values also set the Home printer card's menu and the print-issue list.
- Full-width rows paint over the popover's 1 px border. You can see the breaks in the border in B. To match Figma exactly, the rows would sit 1 px in from the edge.
- The Agent chat's own menus don't use these values at all today; they have their sizes typed into the CSS. I'd switch them to the shared values whichever size you pick, so the composer's + menu matches the header.

**What I'll fix unless you object.** Each of these follows your "Figma wins" ruling:
- **Dark status colours** move to Figma's: success `#4CAF82`, danger `#E07080`, warning `#E8B84A`. The danger text and border on dark buttons repeat the old danger colour by hand, so they change with it. The three separate dark status entries in the token file have no users and get deleted.
- **Buttons.** The Agent page's general-purpose primary button renders 38 high and its secondary 34. Home's primary renders 36. Figma has 34 and 32. I'd bring them in line using the button settings the Agent dialogs already use, which hit 34 and 32 exactly.
- **Text-only link buttons.** On the Agent setup page and the printer panel headers they render 16 to 20 high with no padding, and the setup page's uses the larger 14 px bold font. Figma has 26 high, 4 px side padding, 12 px bold. I'd add a link-button token and use it everywhere.
- **The provider switch on the Agent setup page.** It's the only segmented control, and it renders 34 high with radius 8 and 14 px text. Figma has 30 high, radius 4, 12 px segments. I'd add a token for it.
- **The one custom tooltip** (the revert button's tooltip in the Agent chat) changes to Figma's dark ink tooltip. The other tooltips are the operating system's own and stay as they are.
- **Home's printer dialog** spaces its contents with one-off margins. I'd change it to Figma's 24 padding and 16 gap, which the Agent dialog already uses.
- **The design-system guide** (`design-system.md`) says that when code and Figma disagree, the code wins. Your ruling reverses that, so I'll rewrite that rule.
- **Already the same:** spacing, shadows, text styles, light-mode colours, the reply chip, fields, selects, swatches, status dots and progress bars. Figma's search field doesn't exist in the code yet.

**Why the icon button needs a decision.** A guard test in `test_brand_tokens.cpp:456` requires a text field, a select and an icon button to be the same height, so a field and its reset button line up in a form row. Figma's fields are 26 and its icon button is 32. Moving the icon button to 32 breaks that rule. It also enlarges the header's pane toggles, the canvas tool strip, the reset buttons in tool panels, the print-issue bubble, Home's card menu button and the Agent's Send button.

questions.question: Header chip and menu: which sizes should the shared menu values use (header, Home card menu, print-issue list, and the Agent menus once they adopt them)?

options.label: B: Figma's sizes
options.description: Chip 28, rows 36, popover padding 8, gap 2, rows inset 1 px so the border stays whole. Figma stays as is.

options.label: A: keep today's
options.description: Chip 26, rows 32 with radius 4 and a 4 px inset, padding 4. Figma's Menu/Row, Menu/Popover and chip get changed to match, then the artifact is re-synced.

questions.question: Icon button: Figma has 32, code has 26, and a guard ties fields (26) to the icon button height. What should change?

options.label: 32, keep resets 26 (Recommended)
options.description: Standalone icon buttons (header toggles, tool strip, Send, card menus) go to 32. Reset buttons inside form rows get their own token at field height, and the guard ties them to fields instead.

options.label: 32 everywhere
options.description: Every icon button goes to 32, including reset buttons in form rows, which will then stand taller than the fields beside them. The equality guard is removed.

options.label: Keep 26, change Figma
options.description: Code stays at 26 and Figma's Button/Icon is changed to 26.

questions.question: Eleven colours exist only in the code (secondary and danger button colours, scrim, success-on-action, text-on-action). What should happen to them?

options.label: Map most to Figma (Recommended)
options.description: Secondary and danger buttons use Figma's existing colours: transparent fill, border-subtle, text-primary, status-danger. Visible change: the dark secondary button border goes from strong to subtle. Only scrim and success-on-action have no Figma match; they get added to Figma.

options.label: Add all to Figma
options.description: Keep every code colour as it is and add all eleven to Figma's variables, then re-sync the artifact.

questions.question: Radius names differ (code: standard/compact/container/window/pill; Figma: small/medium/large/chip/full) and pill is 9999 vs full 10. What should change?

options.label: Fix value only (Recommended)
options.description: Rename pill to full and set it to 10. Nothing looks different, because everything using it is 20 px tall or less (inferred from CSS clamping, I'll check it in the app). The other names stay; design-system.md gets a name-mapping table.

options.label: Rename all to Figma

python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
p='resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json'
d=json.load(open(p))
st=d['primitive']['status']
for k in ('successDark','dangerDark','warningDark'): del st[k]
for mode in ('light','dark'):
    s=d['semantic'][mode]
    del s['text']['onAction']
    for k in ('secondary','secondaryHover','secondaryPressed','secondaryText','secondaryBorder','danger','dangerText','dangerBorder'):
        del s['action'][k]
dk=d['semantic']['dark']['status']
dk.update(success='#4CAF82', danger='#E07080', warning='#E8B84A')
d['dimension']['radius']={'small':4,'medium':8,'large':12,'chip':4,'full':10}
c=d['component']
c['button']['icon'].update(width=32,height=32)
c['chip']['height']=28
c['menuRow'].update(height=36, radius=0, sideInset=0)
c['popover'].update(paddingY=8, rowGap=2)
json.dump(d, open(p,'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False); open(p,'a').write('\n')
EOF
git diff --stat

The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
text around it is.

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
  rather than a stripe across it.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in Figma, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate, warning, and info glyphs sit inside a row of Label or Metadata text, 14 to 16 DIP tall, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. The card's disclosure chevron is an ordinary 16 DIP icon. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the Figma frames on the Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

---
name: fake-host-page-fixture
description: "Render the built AgentUI/HomeUI bundles in the built-in browser with a scripted fake native host, to see page states the live app makes hard to catch"
  type: reference
---

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

name: screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture
description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].
